questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which statement about thrombocytopenia is most accurate?
choices: The platelet count alone identifies the cause and treatment
Every low platelet count requires immediate platelet transfusion
Thrombocytopenia is a finding that must be interpreted with bleeding, thrombosis, trends, triggers, and other laboratory data
A normal coagulation panel always proves ITP
questions.explanation: Thrombocytopenia has many causes. Bleeding severity, thrombotic and organ findings, proportional change, smear, hemolysis, coagulation, medications, and triggers determine the likely syndrome and response.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which pattern most strongly suggests acquired TTP?
choices: Thrombocytopenia, schistocytes, hemolysis, and new neurologic change
Isolated mild thrombocytopenia with no symptoms or other abnormalities
Prolonged clotting times after massive trauma without hemolysis assessment
A stable platelet count with an old bruise
questions.explanation: TTP is a thrombotic microangiopathy characterized by thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolysis, and possible neurologic, cardiac, or renal injury. It requires urgent specialist treatment.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient has suspected TTP with confusion, platelets of 18,000/µL, schistocytes, and rising LDH. What is the safest action?
choices: Wait for the complete five-part pentad and final ADAMTS13 result
Activate urgent hematology care and prepare ordered plasma exchange and disease-specific therapy
Give aspirin to prevent microthrombi
Discharge the patient with routine bruising precautions
questions.explanation: Suspected TTP is time-critical. Obtain the ordered ADAMTS13 specimen when feasible, but do not delay hematology-directed plasma exchange and adjunctive therapy while awaiting the result.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which finding pattern is most consistent with DIC?
choices: Stable isolated thrombocytopenia without an underlying illness
Sepsis with oozing from lines, falling platelets and fibrinogen, prolonged clotting times, and worsening organ perfusion
A normal platelet trend after heparin exposure
Petechiae alone with normal serial tests
questions.explanation: DIC is secondary to a major trigger and causes systemic coagulation activation, consumption of platelets and factors, bleeding, thrombosis, and organ injury. Serial trends are essential.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: What is the central treatment priority in DIC?
choices: Treat the underlying cause while supporting perfusion and replacing components only as clinically indicated
Normalize every laboratory value before addressing sepsis or trauma
Give platelets to every patient regardless of bleeding
Avoid serial reassessment after one coagulation panel
questions.explanation: DIC cannot be controlled without treating its cause. Support perfusion and use blood components or anticoagulation selectively according to bleeding, thrombosis, laboratory trends, and specialist guidance.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which heparin-exposed patient has the most concerning HIT pattern?
choices: A 55% platelet fall with a new painful swollen leg and compatible timing
An unchanged platelet count with no thrombosis
A single clumped specimen that normalizes on repeat testing
Minor gum bleeding before heparin was started
questions.explanation: HIT is a prothrombotic disorder. A substantial proportional platelet fall, compatible timing, and new thrombosis raise pretest probability even if the absolute count is not profoundly low.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: The HIT pathway identifies a patient as having suspected HIT. Which action is expected?
choices: Continue heparin flushes because they are a small dose
Stop all heparin sources as ordered and prepare prescribed non-heparin anticoagulation and confirmatory testing
Give warfarin independently before notifying the team
Assume bleeding is the only major risk
questions.explanation: When suspected HIT meets the pathway threshold, all heparin sources are stopped and non-heparin anticoagulation is considered under protocol because thrombosis is the central danger.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which presentation is most typical of ITP?
choices: Isolated thrombocytopenia with petechiae or mucosal bleeding after other causes are excluded
Thrombocytopenia with schistocytes and acute organ ischemia
Sepsis with consumption of platelets and coagulation factors
Heparin exposure followed by new thrombosis
questions.explanation: ITP commonly causes isolated immune thrombocytopenia with variable mucocutaneous bleeding. It remains a diagnosis of exclusion and dangerous mimics must be assessed.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which finding requires immediate emergency response regardless of the current platelet count?
choices: A stable old bruise
Minor petechiae without progression
Sudden severe headache, vomiting, and decreasing level of consciousness
A platelet result pending specimen verification in an asymptomatic patient
questions.explanation: Sudden severe headache and declining consciousness can indicate intracranial bleeding or another neurologic emergency. Patient instability outranks waiting for a numeric threshold.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which trend best indicates improvement during treatment of TTP?
choices: Worsening confusion with new chest pain
Rising LDH with falling hemoglobin and urine output
Stable or rising platelets with resolving hemolysis and improving neurologic and organ function
One higher platelet count despite new focal weakness
questions.explanation: Recovery is multidimensional: platelet count stabilizes while hemolysis, neurologic findings, cardiac or renal injury, and overall organ function improve without new treatment toxicity.
